name: Haircut for face shape
lead: Choosing a haircut for face shape means picking a style that suits the proportions of the face, usually by sorting faces into categories such as oval, round, square, heart or diamond. Stylists and looksmaxxing communities say the right cut can balance the face: adding height or volume where it is narrow, or reducing width where it is broad, so the overall silhouette looks more harmonious.

A general hairstyle reference lists face and head shape, viewed from different angles, among the physical factors that shape a style's appearance, alongside natural hair type, growth patterns, body proportions, the stylist's judgment and the wearer's desired self-image [1]. Facial shape itself is determined mainly by the bones of the face plus soft tissue and is considered a factor in perceived attractiveness [2].
The hairstyle article does not give face-shape-to-haircut rules, and no published study has tested face-shape matching rules.

chain: Identify face shape (oval, round, square and so on)
Choose a cut that adds or reduces width, length or height
Face looks more balanced in proportion
angle.text: A haircut changes the outline around the face, so people use it to make the face look longer, narrower, fuller or more angular. It is among the quickest ways to change how facial proportions read.

infobox: Oval, round, square, heart, diamond, oblong

paras: The idea is that hair can add or reduce visual width, length or angularity so the overall silhouette appears balanced. Stylists commonly sort faces into categories to apply it. The hairstyle article cites face and head shape as one factor alongside natural hair type, growth patterns and the stylist's judgment [1].

Hairstyles are also described as signals of identity, age and social standing, and natural, healthy-looking hair is linked to perceived health, which the same reference suggests helps explain hair's role in attraction [1].

Facial shape is determined mainly by the maxilla, mandible, nasal, zygomatic and frontal bones plus soft tissue, and is considered a factor in perceived attractiveness [2]. That reference contains no research linking face-shape categories to hairstyle selection [2].

Haircut advice features in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums as a cheap upgrade. On T Nation, users posted photos in threads asking for haircut input, and discussed how brow shaping and cut interact [3].

card.summary: Picking a cut by face proportions: a popular styling rule of thumb with no published tests behind it.
card.note: No studies of face-shape matching were found.

quick.overview:
This is the habit of choosing a haircut based on whether your face is oval, round, square and so on.

It is widely used by stylists, but no published studies testing the rules were found.
quick.mechanism: Practitioners say hair length and volume can make a face appear more balanced. Reference sources note that face shape is one of several factors in how a style looks [1].
quick.risks: The practice carries no reported medical risks; the main caveat is that its rules are untested.
